author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Iran-backed Houthi forces have reached Dhubab, a Yemeni town directly on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, two Yemeni government sources told Reuters on Friday. The town sits across the water from Perim island at one of the world’s most consequential maritime chokepoints.

Government sources said control of Dhubab and Perim is important to gaining control over the strait. Bab el-Mandeb links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden, making developments along its shores significant for vessels using routes between Europe and Asia.

Reuters attributed the battlefield update to government sources, and the report did not include an independent on-the-ground verification or a detailed response from the Houthis. The exact extent and durability of the reported advance therefore remained unclear at publication.

The movement is a developing regional-security story because territorial control near the strait can affect military calculations and perceptions of shipping risk even before navigation patterns change. Operators and governments will be watching for confirmation of positions around Dhubab and Perim, statements from the parties, and any effect on maritime traffic. The report follows wider fighting and pressure around Yemen’s Red Sea coast, but this update concerns the forces’ reported arrival at Dhubab specifically.
dek: Two Yemeni government sources told Reuters that Houthi forces reached the coastal town opposite Perim island, placing them at a critical Red Sea chokepoint.
headline: Houthis reach Dhubab on strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, sources say
